title: Modesty
description: Clothing, gender interactions, speech, and gradual growth without cultural pressure.

sections.heading: What to cover day to day
sections.content:
The rules on covering the body (awrah) apply all day, not only in prayer, and they apply to men as well as women.

For men, a Hanafi answer on SeekersGuidance says a man covers from the navel down to and including the knee, at all times unless there is a need. A SeekersGuidance answer on swimming says to go a little past the knee and suggests three-quarter compression pants. Check that sport shorts still cover your knees when you sit, bend or run. If they ride up, wear compression tights underneath.

For women, a SeekersGuidance answer describes the covering in front of men who are not close relatives as everything except the face and hands. The Quran tells believing women to draw their head coverings over their chests (24:31) and to draw their outer garments over themselves (33:59). The schools differ on some smaller details, so ask your teacher which ones apply to you. The modesty and clothing guide has a section on starting hijab.

Covering also means clothing that is not see-through and not so tight that it shows the shape underneath. The SeekersGuidance answer on women's swimming, for example, asks for loose clothing that is not thin.

Both men and women are told to lower their gaze (24:30-31). A particular cultural garment is not the requirement. The covering is, and that is the target. If you cannot reach it everywhere yet, keep the step you can hold and plan the rest with a teacher.

sections.heading: Modesty is broader than clothing
sections.content: Modesty covers clothing, gaze, speech, behavior, humility, and dignity. Clothing is part of it and not the whole of it. Learn what modesty is for first, then take steps you can keep up.

sections.heading: Gradual clothing changes
sections.content: Start with what you can maintain: looser clothing, outfits you can pray in, or more coverage in settings where that is safe. Do not buy a whole wardrobe in a panic. Ask a qualified teacher what is required and which details can wait.

sections.heading: Culture and pressure
sections.content: Muslim cultures have different clothing styles. You may like the look of one of them, and liking it does not make it required for you. Be careful around people who shame you, compare you harshly, or treat visible changes as the only measure of faith.

sections.heading: Family, work, and safety
sections.content: Visible changes can affect how family reacts, and they can affect work or school. If a change might create hostility or danger, talk to a trusted local mentor before moving quickly. For workplace or school concerns, get qualified local guidance instead of relying on generic advice.
